qaoa_key_conditions.execution: Classical noisy simulation using IBM FakeBrisbane-derived device noise. No physical QPU, annealer or strong industrial/classical-solver runtime benchmark.

conditions.representative_early_termination: Allowed when its target is reached; actual effort can differ from the full maximum used by independent branch training.
conditions.initialization: Physics-informed shortcut near gamma=-pi/6,beta=-pi/8 is another component; the source explicitly distinguishes its Ising convention from standard MaxCut angle conventions.
conditions.hardware_for_simulation: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO5955WX16-core CPU,512GB RAM,three NVIDIA RTX4090 GPUs.

Table4_m3.means_scope: Dataset-averaged values across reported node instances; the table supplies no per-cell uncertainty/error bars.

qualifications: ARG is100*abs((Emin-<Hc>)/Emin), a mean-energy relative gap, not optimum-bitstring yield or solution-success probability.

The headline shot ratios about285–386 and times about6.5–23.9 combine actual training effort, informed initialization/early termination, target-specific refinement and branch evaluation. The source explicitly does not isolate parameter-transfer-only causation.
Replacing8 full branch trainings by1 changes that component by8 at matched full-training budgets, before other costs. It does not explain386 alone, constant total cost or exponential speedup in N.
At m2, Regular49vs48,SK61vs59 andAIDS44vs42 have higher DO gaps. The original DQB correctly preserves this counterexample.
Matching/beating FrozenQubits at m3 does not mean beating every baseline: HEA mean ARG37vsDO57 onSK and40vs42 onRegular. No uncertainty-based significance rank can be inferred.
No matched industrial constraint/whole-workflow time-to-target result is established. CP-SAT/local-search comparison in the DQB is an editorial future-test proposal.

rydberg_key_conditions.execution: Reanalysis of experimental projective measurements from the earlier256-atom Rydberg experiment plus new classical neural guiding/PQMC calculations. Actual hardware data are an input; the final ground-state calculation is classical continuous-time PQMC.
rydberg_key_conditions.physical_scope: Open-boundary16x16 array of87Rb, Rb/a about1.15,Omega=2*pi*4.3MHz,interaction cutoff4a. A global z-axis rotation makes the model stoquastic, enabling sign-problem-free positive-amplitude PQMC. This does not solve generic fermionic/sign/phase problems.

dataset.source_reference: S. Ebadi et al., Quantum phases of matter on a256-atom programmable quantum simulator, Nature595,227(2021); dataset handling follows M. S. Moss et al., Phys.Rev.A109,032410(2024). These cited papers were identified in the new source bibliography; their fulltexts were not freshly reread.
dataset.augmentation: Original plus pi/2,pi,3pi/2 lattice rotations gives16000 training configurations perdetuning; not16000 independent hardware shots.
dataset.smaller_sizes: L8/L12 configurations are crops of the availableL16 measurements, not new quantum-device experiments at those sizes.
dataset.hardware_readout_fidelity_reported: about99%, as listed in Table2; not independently remeasured.

architectures.interpretation: The more expressive/effective patched RNN reaches the SSE uncertainty band with fewer walkers even without experimental pretraining than the data-pretrained RBM. Data initialization still adds a smaller RNN benefit; compare against the stronger classical guide.

metrics: The reference in Fig2 and subsequent main energy comparisons is stochastic-series-expansion ground-state energy with statistical uncertainty. Fig3 instead uses the corresponding method's Nw10000 mixed-estimator energy as reference; do not label all its points independent SSE benchmarks.

Energy uses the converged mixed estimator. Checkerboard order/noncommuting observables require separate forward-walking pure estimators; no claim that a mixed estimate is unbiased for arbitrary observables.

Experimental configurations deviate from ideal equilibrium, especially ordered-phase order parameters. Their usefulness as initialization does not certify that the hardware already prepared the target ground state.
Unbiased/exact ground-state statements refer to converged projection/large-population limits. Finite walker budgets have controlled residual bias checked against the stated references.

Finite-size critical-property validation was run without experimental-data pretraining, separating classical-method reliability from the data enhancement. Current text/table andFig7caption report slightly different fit summaries; do not add exact critical values to the briefing without edition/locator qualification.

Table5_step_times_s.boundary: Per-step timings on different devices and code paths, not a measured full-workflow speedup, matched hardware comparison or quantum advantage. Data acquisition, all training/projection/reuse and hardware access costs need a matched target-budget comparison.
